description: How banks, microfinance institutions and fintech firms measure and control market, credit, liquidity, operational, counterparty and model risk. Students estimate value at risk, build credit scorecards, run stress tests and produce a regulatory-style risk report on portfolios drawn from Ghanaian and regional markets.
modelledOn: Hull, Risk Management and Financial Institutions
McNeil, Frey and Embrechts, Quantitative Risk Management
Basel Committee on Banking Supervision, Basel Framework standards
Jorion, Value at Risk: The New Benchmark for Managing Financial Risk
outcomes: Compute and backtest value at risk and expected shortfall with parametric, historical and Monte Carlo methods.
Build and validate a credit scorecard and estimate expected and unexpected credit loss for a loan portfolio.
Model liquidity and operational loss exposures, including mobile-money float and fraud scenarios.
Design macroeconomic stress scenarios and translate them into portfolio losses and capital impact.
Quantify counterparty exposure and the effect of netting and collateral.
Assess model risk and prepare a risk report that links measured risk to regulatory capital.

units.title: Risk foundations and measures
topics: Risk taxonomy: market, credit, liquidity, operational, counterparty and model risk; risk versus uncertainty
Returns and stylised facts: log returns, volatility clustering and fat tails
Risk measures: variance, value at risk, expected shortfall and the coherence axioms
Risk governance: three lines of defence, risk appetite and limits

units.title: Market risk
topics: Parametric (delta-normal) value at risk and the variance-covariance method
Historical simulation, filtered historical simulation and Monte Carlo value at risk
Volatility models: EWMA and GARCH(1,1)
Extreme value theory: peaks over threshold and the generalised Pareto tail
Backtesting: Kupiec proportion-of-failures test, Christoffersen independence test and the traffic-light approach
Portfolio risk: factor models, marginal and component value at risk, and exchange-rate exposure to the cedi
Interest rate risk: duration, convexity, DV01 and key rate durations

units.title: Credit risk
topics: Probability of default, loss given default and exposure at default; expected and unexpected loss
Scorecards: logistic regression, weight of evidence, information value, Gini and KS statistics for microloans
Structural (Merton) and reduced-form models of default
Portfolio credit risk: the Vasicek single-factor model, default correlation and credit value at risk
IFRS 9 expected credit loss: staging and forward-looking provisions
Rating migration matrices and Markov chain transition models

units.title: Liquidity and operational risk
topics: Funding and market liquidity: bid-ask costs, liquidity-adjusted value at risk, liquidity coverage and net stable funding ratios
Runs and float risk in mobile money and savings institutions
Operational risk: the loss distribution approach with frequency and severity models
Fraud and cyber loss scenarios and key risk indicators
Business continuity, incident response and risk transfer through insurance

units.title: Stress testing and scenario analysis
topics: Sensitivity analysis, scenario analysis and reverse stress testing
Macroeconomic scenario design: commodity prices for cocoa, gold and oil, currency depreciation and rate shocks
Satellite models linking macroeconomic variables to default rates and losses
Governance of stress tests: management actions, documentation and board challenge
Case study: sovereign debt restructuring and its effect on bank balance sheets

units.title: Counterparty risk and collateral
topics: Exposure profiles: expected exposure, potential future exposure and expected positive exposure
Credit valuation adjustment and wrong-way risk
Netting, close-out and master agreements
Collateral and margin: variation and initial margin, haircuts and central counterparties
Settlement risk and payment systems

units.title: Model risk and validation
topics: Sources of model risk: specification, estimation, implementation and use
Validation practice: conceptual soundness, outcome analysis, benchmarking and back-testing
Model inventory, tiering, documentation and governance
Parameter uncertainty and model averaging
Machine learning in risk models: explainability, drift and challenger models
Case studies of model failures and the lessons for governance

units.title: Regulatory capital and risk reporting
topics: The Basel framework: three pillars, capital ratios and risk-weighted assets
Standardised and internal ratings-based approaches, the Vasicek capital formula and the fundamental review of the trading book
Prudential requirements of the central bank in Ghana and the region, and how local rules differ from Basel
ICAAP, risk dashboards and board reporting
Capstone: a risk report for a bank or microfinance loan and trading portfolio

schedule.title: Risk taxonomy, returns and risk measures
schedule.exercise: Compute volatility, value at risk and expected shortfall for one daily return series and write a short note on why VaR is not coherent.

tasks.title: Load two years of daily cedi exchange rates, compute log returns and test for fat tails with a QQ plot and kurtosis
Compute 99 percent VaR and expected shortfall for a normal and a fat-tailed return distribution and compare the two
Set risk limits and escalation rules for a trading desk in a governance case and score your design against the rubric

schedule.title: Parametric and simulation-based value at risk
schedule.exercise: Compare delta-normal, historical and Monte Carlo VaR for a portfolio of a cedi bond and a dollar position, and explain the differences in the three numbers.

tasks.title: Compute delta-normal one-day 99 percent VaR for a two-asset portfolio from a covariance matrix and decompose it by asset
Compute historical and Monte Carlo VaR for the same portfolio from 500 days of data and compare with the parametric result
Implement filtered historical simulation using GARCH standardised residuals and show how VaR reacts to a volatility spike

schedule.title: Volatility models, extremes and backtesting
schedule.exercise: Backtest a 99 percent VaR model over 250 days, count exceptions, run the Kupiec and independence tests and decide whether to keep the model.

tasks.title: Fit an EWMA with lambda 0.94 and a GARCH(1,1) to a return series and plot both conditional volatilities against realised volatility
Fit a generalised Pareto tail to the worst 5 percent of losses and estimate the 99.9 percent VaR from the tail
Run the Kupiec and Christoffersen tests on 500 days of VaR exceptions and assign the Basel traffic-light zone

schedule.title: Portfolio risk and interest rate risk
schedule.exercise: Report the main risk contributors for a bank's treasury book, and propose a hedge that reduces the largest contributor.

tasks.title: Compute modified duration, DV01 and convexity for a 5-year government bond and estimate price change for a 100 basis point shock
Decompose portfolio VaR into component contributions across four positions and identify which position adds most risk
Hedge a dollar receivable against cedi depreciation with a forward and compare hedged and unhedged loss distributions by simulation

schedule.title: Credit risk measures and scorecards
schedule.exercise: Compute expected loss for a loan book from PD, LGD and EAD by segment, and explain why unexpected loss needs capital.

tasks.title: Compute expected loss for five loan segments given PD, LGD and EAD and rank them by contribution to the total
Build a mobile-money loan scorecard with weight of evidence bins and logistic regression, then report Gini and KS on a hold-out set
Compute Merton distance to default and implied default probability for a firm from equity value, volatility and debt

schedule.title: Portfolio credit risk, provisioning and migration
schedule.exercise: Prepare an IFRS 9 provisioning note for a microfinance book, assigning loans to stages and computing the twelve-month and lifetime expected credit loss.

tasks.title: Raise a rating migration matrix to powers to get multi-year default probabilities and read off five-year cumulative default
Simulate the Vasicek single-factor model for 1,000 loans and estimate the 99.9 percent credit VaR for two asset correlations
Stage a loan portfolio by days past due and a significant increase in risk, compute lifetime ECL and compare with a flat provision

schedule.title: Liquidity and operational risk
schedule.exercise: Write a risk assessment of a mobile-money operator covering float, agent liquidity, fraud losses and continuity, with three key risk indicators.

tasks.title: Simulate daily withdrawals and deposits at 20 mobile-money agents and estimate the float needed to keep stock-outs below 1 percent
Fit frequency and severity distributions to operational loss data and compute annual 99.9 percent operational VaR by Monte Carlo
Respond to a mobile-money fraud incident in a branching case, choose containment and reporting steps and score against the rubric

schedule.title: Stress testing and scenarios
schedule.exercise: Design a severe but plausible scenario with a cocoa price collapse and a 30 percent cedi depreciation, and trace its effect on a bank's capital ratio.

tasks.title: Apply a parallel 300 basis point rate shock to a bank balance sheet and compute the change in economic value of equity
Fit a regression of default rates on GDP growth and the exchange rate and use it to project losses under a stress scenario
Choose management actions for a bank facing a domestic debt exchange in a case and score the capital outcome against the rubric

schedule.title: Counterparty risk and collateral
schedule.exercise: Show with a worked example how netting and collateral reduce exposure between two banks, and compute the residual exposure.

tasks.title: Simulate exposure paths for a currency forward and plot expected exposure and 95 percent potential future exposure over its life
Compute exposure with and without netting for a portfolio of six trades with a counterparty and report the reduction
Compute a credit valuation adjustment from an exposure profile and a hazard rate, then show the effect of wrong-way risk

schedule.title: Model risk and validation practice
schedule.exercise: Write a validation report for a credit scorecard, covering conceptual soundness, data, performance, stability and your recommendation.

tasks.title: Review a model change request in a governance case, identify the model risks and score your approval conditions against the rubric
Validate a credit scorecard by comparing its Gini on development and out-of-time samples and benchmarking against a challenger model
Assign risk tiers and review frequencies to a model inventory of twelve models in a case and score against the rubric

schedule.title: Uncertainty, machine learning and failures
schedule.exercise: Analyse a model failure case and write a half-page lesson for the risk committee covering cause, early signs and governance changes.

tasks.title: Bootstrap the parameters of a VaR model and show how much the 99 percent VaR changes across the resampled estimates
Compare a gradient-boosted default model with a scorecard on discrimination, stability and explainability, and decide which to approve
Investigate a failed risk model case, rank the causes from the evidence and score your recommendations against the rubric

schedule.title: Regulatory capital
schedule.exercise: Compute a bank's capital ratios under the standardised approach from an exposure table, and say how much capital headroom remains after a stress.

tasks.title: Compute risk-weighted assets and the capital adequacy ratio for a bank from a table of exposures and risk weights
Compute the internal-ratings-based capital requirement with the Vasicek formula for four PD and LGD pairs and compare with the standardised approach
Choose a capital plan for a regional bank in a case that must satisfy local and Basel minima, and score against the rubric

schedule.title: Risk reporting and capstone
schedule.exercise: Present the capstone risk report for a bank or microfinance portfolio with VaR, credit loss, liquidity, stress results and recommendations.

tasks.title: Build a board risk dashboard with limit utilisation, VaR trend and top concentrations and flag the three most urgent breaches
Run market, credit and liquidity calculations on a supplied portfolio and combine them in a summary table with a capital impact
Present your risk report to a simulated board, answer challenges and score your recommendations against the rubric
